topic: Mohe 1997 gravity anomaly — verification of ISS-2687 patch (bound clause scope: 'any such anomalous coupling' -> 'gravitational shielding')
our_argument_summary: WIN-011 (verdict: Not Demonstrated) documents the dome silently rewriting its Mohe-1997 gravity claim from -6.5 uGal at eclipse maximum to ~7.0 +/- 2.7 uGal at first/last contact (where Wang et al. 2000 had put the data), with the WIN-012 coupling constant still using the superseded 6.5, and the dome conceding the thermal-tilt loophole pending an August 2026 SG test. The Unnikrishnan passage argues the dome cites its chosen authority selectively: the paper rules out both shielding AND new gravitational properties.

patches.target: detail_evidence bound-clause scope fix per c12 H1

ISS-2687.evidence: Diff of wins.json between 3eb437a^ and 3eb437a shows exactly one change to WIN-011: 'tightest terrestrial bound ever measured on any such anomalous coupling' -> '...on gravitational shielding' in detail_evidence. This is precisely c12 H1's recommended fix: the paper's quantitative bound parameterizes the gravitational shielding (Majorana extinction) parameter specifically — c11's search evidence quoted the paper constraining 'the characteristic shielding parameter to the lowest bound ever from a terrestrial experiment'. detail_evidence length moved 7851 -> 7847 (-4 chars), confirming a surgical single-clause edit with no collateral changes. Stale phrase count is now 0 across wins.json, sections.json, and docs/index.html; the corrected phrase appears once in the built docs/index.html — no build drift.

over_narrowing_check: Confirmed NOT over-narrowed. The 'rule out both' clause survives intact under the data-as-evidence framing c12 endorsed, and the two sentences that follow still carry the new-property-of-gravitation argument explicitly: the dome's electromagnetic-gravitational coupling IS a claim of a new property of gravitation, and the paper 'rules out the 1997 data as evidence for the dome's mechanism in the same breath'. Narrowing only the numerical-bound clause to shielding makes the sentence match what the paper actually quantifies while the selective-citation argument retains full force. A defender can no longer say we attached the bound to a coupling the paper never parameterized; nothing the dome could exploit was conceded.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's offensive use of Unnikrishnan et al. (2001, Phys. Rev. D 63, 062002) against the globe shielding hypothesis is, on its face, a fair citation (data/wins.json:WIN-011 detail_evidence — our own text credits this and corrects an earlier version of our review that called it self-defeating).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The citation is selective: the paper's stated purpose was to test shielding OR 'some new property of gravitation', and it rules out both — the bound on gravitational shielding plus the conclusion that the 1997 record evidences no anomalous signal of either kind (data/wins.json:WIN-011 detail_evidence, post-ISS-2687 text). The dome cites the half that wounds its competitor and omits the half that wounds itself.

summary_for_decider: Queue-517 patch VERIFIED: ISS-2687 implemented c12 H1's recommendation exactly (single-clause scope fix, -4 chars, no collateral edits, no build drift, stale phrase fully purged). Over-narrowing check passed — the selective-citation argument and 'rule out both' framing remain fully supported by surrounding text. c12 residual is RESOLVED; zero holes this cycle. WIN-011 is clean at c13. Code tags carried forward validly (poller SHA for monitor.py unchanged). Note for cross-page coherence: the companion section 4.2.4 gamma-bound appositive (queue 515, ISS-2673) was verified separately by curmudgeon-verify c2 with 0 holes; WIN-011's 'tightest terrestrial bound' phrasing and section 4.2.4's 'broadly consistent with prior eclipse estimates' phrasing are compatible (tighter than, and compared against, prior spring-gravimeter bounds — not contradictory).
deeper_analysis: Adversarial angles considered and dismissed: (1) Could a defender attack 'tightest terrestrial bound ever measured' as potentially superseded post-2001? The phrase predates this patch, reflects the paper's own self-description, and any tighter subsequent bound would strengthen, not weaken, our argument against the dome's coupling — no exploitable hole. (2) Could narrowing to 'gravitational shielding' let the dome say its EM-coupling escapes the paper entirely? No — the immediately following sentences carry that weight through the paper's qualitative conclusion on 'some new property of gravitation', which is the correct attachment point; that was the entire asymmetry c11 H1/c12 H1 worked to fix. (3) Verified the fingerprint delta (7851->7847) matches the exact character arithmetic of the swap (27->23 chars), ruling out any unlogged edits to the field.
